chunks: Saad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Ali ibn Hanzalah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the last two rak'ahs, what should I do in them? He said: 'If you wish, recite the Opening of the Book (Al-Fatiha); and if you wish, remember Allah, for they are equal.' I said: 'Which of these is better?' He said: 'They are equal, by Allah. If you wish, you glorify (say Subhanallah); and if you wish, you recite.'
As for what Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated regarding the preference of recitation over glorification, the intended meaning is when the person is an Imam (leading the prayer).
ai.seo_question: What should I recite or say in the last two rak'ahs of prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies that in the last two rak'ahs, reciting Al-Fatiha or engaging in dhikr are equally valid, resolving apparent contradictions in other narrations by specifying that the preference for recitation applies primarily when one is leading the prayer as an Imam. This distinction highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding voluntary acts of worship, emphasizing that the spiritual merit remains consistent regardless of the chosen method. The ruling underscores the practical ease granted to worshippers while maintaining the structural integrity of the prayer.
